title: Machine-readable commands for the local client
requirements: Every operation the local client shows must be reachable as a parameterized `forgel` subcommand that needs no interactive prompt: free text, project status, milestone status, task list, accept a task, reject a task, retry a task, run the daemon now, pause, resume, plan a milestone from a goal, list projects, select the active project.

Free text sent by the user must have a single engine entry point (`forgel say`) that returns the same structured outcome as the chat router: an answer, a queued task, a plan, or a control action, with the reply text.
Each of those subcommands must accept `--json` and then write exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else; without the flag the existing human-readable text stays the output.

The JSON object must carry a stable envelope: a success flag, a kind, the reply text and the operation-specific payload; a failed call must exit with a non-zero status and still return one JSON object describing the error.

The active project must be a durable session on the engine side, addressable by a session key that defaults to `local`, so the client stays stateless between calls. Commands to set and read the session are required.
Free text must go through the same router logic that console and Telegram use; no duplicated dispatch table and no second implementation of the same command in the CLI layer.
The recent conversation of a session must be readable as a command that returns it in JSON, so the client can show a short history without reading project files.
Existing behaviour must not change: `forgel chat`, `forgel telegram`, `forgel`, the interactive commands and their texts keep working as before, and the existing test suite stays green.
Document the command set and the JSON envelope in the public docs (README and the relevant section of PLAN.md) so the future client repository can rely on a written contract.
Add `unittest` tests that assert the JSON envelope for each new command, the error envelope and exit codes, and that `forgel say` routes a change request to a queued task in script model mode.
acceptance: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes and includes new tests for the command interface.
Each new subcommand with `--json` prints exactly one JSON object and exits 0 on success, verified by a test.
A failing call exits non-zero and prints one JSON object with an error description, verified by a test.
With script model mode, `forgel say --project <id> --json --text "add a health endpoint"` returns a JSON object with kind `change_request` and the queued task id, verified by a test.

`forgel status <id> --json`, `forgel tasks <id> --json`, `forgel task accept --json`, `forgel task reject --json`, `forgel task retry --json`, `forgel plan --status --json` and `forgel projects --json` are covered by tests and documented.
The session commands set and read the active project for a session key and default to `local`, covered by a test.
Existing console and Telegram tests still pass unchanged.
constraints: Do not move the console yet and do not delete the chat mode in this task; that is the next step.
Do not let the CLI layer reimplement routing: it must call the existing router and core functions.
Public artifacts (docs, commit messages, code identifiers) in English, commits signed off.
The JSON envelope must be documented, not just implemented, and must not leak secrets.
assumptions: The session key defaults to `local`, matching the console's chat id 0, and is passed with `--session` when another value is needed.
The free-text entry point is named `forgel say` and takes the text with `--text` (or as the trailing argument) plus `--project`.
With `--json`, stdout carries only the JSON object; human text goes to stdout only without the flag.
The envelope is flat at the top level: `ok`, `kind`, `text`, `error`, plus an operation-specific field such as `task`, `tasks`, `plan`, `project`, `projects` or `history`.
The work stays in the `main` repository; the client repository is created in the following step.

result.summary:
Доработал предыдущую реализацию по двум замечаниям ревью.

1. Флаг `--json` теперь действительно управляет выводом. В `src/forgel/client_cli.py` добавлены `emit()` и `fail()`: с `--json` в stdout уходит ровно один JSON-объект, без флага печатается человекочитаемый `text` (для ошибок — сообщение в stderr, stdout пустой). Хелперы применены во всех командах — say, projects, session, use, history, tasks, status, task, plan, pause, resume, daemon; `write()` остался только для внутреннего вывода конверта.
2. Публичная документация обновлена. В README.md появился раздел «Scripted Client» с набором команд и таблицей конверта (и ссылка из «One Client»), в PLAN.md добавлен раздел §7.18 «Machine-Readable Client Commands» с конвертом, правилами `say`, сессиями и совместимостью; docs/program/commands.md приведён к тому же контракту.

Новые тесты в tests/test_client.py: `test_without_json_the_human_readable_text_is_printed` (tasks/projects/say/session/history без флага печатают текст, а не JSON) и `test_failing_call_without_json_prints_no_object` (ошибка без флага — ненулевой код и пустой stdout). Остальные тесты предыдущей итерации (конверт каждой команды, ошибка с одним JSON и ненулевым кодом, сессии с ключом по умолчанию `local`, история, `say` с маршрутизацией `change_request` в очередь в script-режиме) сохранены. Полный прогон `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — 529 тестов, OK, включая существующие console/Telegram тесты без изменений.

review.summary: The change adds a machine-readable client command surface (src/forgel/client.py + client_cli.py) wired into entry.main before the legacy CLI, sharing CommandRouter through the new outcome.handle_outcome so `forgel say` reports answer/change_request/plan/action with the router's reply text, plus a durable engine-side session with default key `local` (session.py), JSON envelope (ok/kind/text/error + payload), a history command backed by the project conversation store, and documentation in README, docs/program/commands.md and PLAN.md. Existing commands (chat, telegram, bare forgel, task/status/plan/pause/resume/daemon without --json) keep the legacy path, no third-party dependencies were added, and the attributed tests plus reported acceptance checks (environment test/e2e, unittest discover) pass. No test removals were detected and no secrets are exposed in the documented payload.

requirements.requirement: Every local-client operation is reachable as a parameterized non-interactive `forgel` subcommand (free text, project status, milestone status, task list, accept/reject/retry a task, run the daemon, pause, resume, plan a milestone, list projects, select the active project).
requirements.note: client.py builds say/tasks/status/task accept|reject|retry/plan/projects/pause/resume/daemon/session/use/history; plan --status and project status are covered; core functions (accept_task, reject_task, plan_project, plan_status, run_daemon, set_paused) are called rather than duplicated.

requirements.requirement: Free text has a single engine entry point (`forgel say`) that returns the same structured outcome as the chat router: answer, queued task, plan or control action, with the reply text.
requirements.note: client_cli.say delegates to outcome.handle_outcome, which calls CommandRouter.handle and classifies via _Recorder into answer/change_request/action/plan, carrying reply.text.

requirements.requirement: Each new subcommand accepts `--json` and writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else; without the flag the human-readable text remains the output.
requirements.note: emit() prints json.dumps(dict) only with --json and otherwise prints the text; fail() writes one envelope; tests strip lines and assert a single JSON line via _call().

requirements.requirement: Stable JSON envelope with success flag, kind, reply text and operation-specific payload; a failed call exits non-zero and still returns one JSON object describing the error.
requirements.note: envelope(ok, kind, text, error, **payload) is flat; fail() prints 'error: ...' to stderr, writes one ok:false object when --json and returns 1. A usage parse error also emits one JSON object with --json.

requirements.requirement: The active project is a durable engine-side session addressable by a session key defaulting to `local`, with commands to set and read it.
requirements.note: session.py stores the selection in the ledger, DEFAULT_SESSION = 'local' mapping to chat id 0, with get/set/clear, session_view and conversation; client_cli exposes `session` (read/set) and `use` (set), and `--session` switches the key.

requirements.requirement: Free text goes through the same router logic as console and Telegram; no duplicated dispatch table and no second implementation in the CLI layer.
requirements.note: say constructs a CommandRouter (with the model-built ProjectAgent when available) and calls outcome.handle_outcome; no CLI-side re-implementation of routing exists, only core function calls for reporting/control commands.

requirements.requirement: Recent conversation of a session is readable as a JSON command without reading project files directly.
requirements.note: `forgel history` calls session.conversation, which loads the project history via agent.load_history and returns role/text/at rows through the envelope's `history` payload.

requirements.requirement: Existing behaviour is unchanged: `forgel chat`, `forgel telegram`, `forgel`, the interactive commands and their texts keep working, and the existing test suite stays green.
requirements.note: maybe_dispatch only intercepts the six new names unconditionally and the other commands only when `--json` is present; otherwise entry.main falls through to cli.main. Reported acceptance checks (environment test/e2e, task test command) pass and no tests were removed.

requirements.requirement: Document the command set and JSON envelope in the public docs (README and the relevant PLAN.md section), with the contract not leaking secrets.
requirements.note: README gained a 'Scripted Client' section with the command list and envelope table; docs/program/commands.md records the full contract; PLAN.md is among the attributed files. The documented payload fields (task/tasks/plan/project/projects/history/paused/cycles) carry no secrets.

requirements.requirement: Add unittest tests asserting the JSON envelope for each new command, the error envelope and exit codes, and that `forgel say` routes a change request to a queued task in script model mode.
requirements.note: tests/test_client.py drives entry.main under FORGEL_MODEL_MODE=script, asserts a single JSON line and envelope fields (status, tasks, task accept, etc.) and uses accept/reject/retry/plan/projects/session helpers; the reported task test command passes, satisfying the acceptance tests.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes; each new subcommand with --json prints one object and exits 0; a failing call exits non-zero with one error object; say returns kind change_request with queued task id; status/tasks/task accept|reject|retry/plan --status/projects covered and documented; session set/read defaults to `local`.
requirements.note: The environment/task test command and e2e checks passed (exit 0), and the attributed test file provides the envelope helper and per-command coverage for the required operations and the default-`local` session.

requirements.requirement: Constraints: do not move the console or delete chat mode; do not reimplement routing; no new third-party dependencies; public artifacts in English; commits signed off.
requirements.note: console.py/chat.py stay intact and entry.main still falls back to cli.main; no new pip dependencies were introduced; docs and identifiers are English; both attributed commits carry the Signed-off-by trailer.

feedback: review: Public documentation requirement not met: README.md and PLAN.md were not updated with the command set and JSON envelope; only a new docs/program/commands.md was added.

review: The `--json` flag is not honoured for the new commands: say/projects/session/use/history/tasks always print the JSON envelope, so without the flag the documented human-readable output is not produced.

review summary: The command surface itself is implemented well: client.py parses say/status/tasks/task/projects/session/use/history/plan/pause/resume/daemon, client_cli.py builds one flat envelope with a non-zero exit and a single JSON error object, outcome.py observes the existing CommandRouter instead of adding a second dispatch table, and session.py makes the selected project a durable engine-side session defaulting to `local` (ledger chat id 0). The attributed change does, however, miss two stated requirements: the public docs were not updated (README.md and PLAN.md are untouched; only a new docs/program/commands.md was added), and the `--json` flag is not actually honoured by the new commands, which always print the JSON envelope on stdout and only ever gate the pre-existing commands. Everything else (acceptance checks, script-mode `say` routing, error envelope, sessions, no new dependencies, signed-off commit) looks in order.
